# DMPG-retningslinje

DMPG-retningslinje is mentioned once in the corpus in connection with ongoing work on developing guidelines for "social screening" as part of assessing patients' social support needs [^src1]. The name refers to a guideline-development effort (retningslinje means "guideline" in Danish), likely tied to a body abbreviated DMPG, though no further identification of this organization is given in the available data.

This single mention appears in the context of a discussion of Indicator 10 from the ADHD database, which measures the proportion of treatment courses among adults where the patient's social support needs were assessed within 120 days of treatment start. This was the first time this indicator had been reported, and results showed substantial shortfalls against the 90% quality target — 37% nationally and a range of 14–52% across regions [^src1]. The steering group (styregruppen) discussed the reasons for the low fulfilment rate, including registration practices and data quality from child and adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinics and private hospitals, and decided to work on improving registration practices [^src1]. The forthcoming work by DMPG-retningslinje on "social screening" is referenced as part of this broader effort to improve how social support needs are assessed and documented.

No further details — relationships, claims, or timeline events — are available for this entity in the corpus.
